config.theme: Sprint planning for a payments team at a fictional fintech
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Sprint planning for a payments team at a fictional fintech

personas.name: Rachel
personas.hidden_agenda: Her skip-level asked why the team keeps missing

personas.name: Dev
personas.goals: Do the PCI fixes before the auditors come back
personas.hidden_agenda: Thinks product doesn't understand the audit risk

personas.name: Carmen
personas.goals: Ship the chargeback flow this sprint
personas.hidden_agenda: Promised two big merchants a date

personas.name: Oskar
personas.role: Engineer, carries most of the on-call

agenda.title: Last sprint review
agenda.goal: Be honest about what shipped and what didn't

agenda.title: Sprint scope
agenda.goal: Choose between the chargeback flow and the PCI audit fixes

agenda.title: Estimates
agenda.goal: Size the chosen work and check it fits

agenda.title: Team health and on-call
agenda.goal: Sort out the on-call load and the hiring gap

beats.summary: The miss; Carmen remembers the delivery as better than it was
Chargebacks vs PCI; a shouting match; Dev overstates the PCI findings and Rachel catches it much later
Sizing; a running joke about Oskar's sourdough takes over for a bit
On-call load, hiring and Oskar's job offer

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Okay, real talk. Last sprint we committed forty-five points and we did not get close.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: We got most of it, though. Like thirty-eight?

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: The board says twenty-nine.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Twenty-nine? Hang on, that can't include the dispute API work.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: It includes it. It was split across two tickets and one didn't close.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: The two P1s didn't help. Each one ate a day of somebody.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: The reality is we plan like nobody gets paged and then everybody gets paged.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Okay but that's every team.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: It's not every team. Most teams don't own card authorization.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Ugh, Slack is on fire over here. Ignore my face.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Hang on, let's not do this again. The question is what we change.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Plan for the pages. That's what we change.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: How many pages were there, Oskar?

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Twenty-three. Most of them at night.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Twenty-three? That's insane.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Sure. It was.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Okay. Then this sprint we plan to what we actually delivered, not what we wish we'd delivered.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: I mean, that's the first sensible thing anyone's said about planning all year.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Scope. Carmen, you want the chargeback flow.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Merchants are screaming. We had seventeen escalations about chargebacks last month.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: And we have ten open PCI findings. Auditors don't scream, they just fail you.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Okay but the chargeback rate is like two percent. We're paying for every one of them.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: What did chargebacks actually cost us last month?

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Fourteen thousand two hundred in fees. Every month this doesn't ship.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: PCI remediation is due December fifteenth. That's a hard date with real consequences.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: The merchants' date is a hard date too! I told Pivot Coffee and Brightline—

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: You told them a date?

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: I told them "this quarter". Roughly.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: The reality is, "roughly" is how we got here.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Don't make this about me, Dev.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: I'm making it about the audit.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Can we do half and half?

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Half of each usually means none of either.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Sure. Whatever works.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Okay, real talk. Which of the PCI findings actually block the audit?

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: The ones about key rotation and the log retention. Those are the scary ones.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: So not all of them are scary.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: I mean, they're all findings. Some are scarier.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Hang on. Then we do the scary PCI ones first, and the chargeback flow gets whatever's left.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Whatever's left is nothing. You know it's nothing.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Hang on, I just pulled up the audit tracker. It's six open findings, not ten.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Six. Okay, six. Still.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Six, of which two are scary. Okay. Key rotation and log retention, then the chargeback flow, in that order. That's the scope. Decided.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Fine. But I'm writing down that it's on you if Brightline churns.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Write it down. I'll talk to Brightline myself if it comes to that.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Sure.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Estimates. Dev, key rotation.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Eight points. Maybe thirteen if the HSM vendor is slow again.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: The vendor is always slow.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: How big is the chargeback flow, honestly?

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: The reality is, it's two sprints of work if we do it right.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Then we do a first version. Merchants just need the evidence upload.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Could the evidence upload alone fit this sprint?

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Probably.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: If nobody gets paged. So, no.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Unrelated, but my sourdough starter died this weekend.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Oskar. You named that thing.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Gerald. His name was Gerald.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: I mean, I'm sorry for your loss.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Okay, can we bury Gerald after planning?

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: So the evidence upload, is it in or out?

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Hang on. Five engineers, two open roles, a week of on-call each. It's in, as a stretch goal, behind the PCI work. Okay, that's the call.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: A stretch goal. Fine. I'll write the evidence upload ticket today so it's ready if there's room.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Last thing. Team. Oskar, you took most of the pages again.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Sure. It's fine.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: It's not fine. You look terrible. No offense.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Some taken.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Real talk, should we change the rotation so nobody does back-to-back weeks?

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Yes. Obviously yes.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Then no back-to-back on-call weeks, starting this sprint.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: I'll redo the on-call schedule tonight so Oskar's off next week.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Thanks, Dev.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Where are we on the two open roles?

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: One final round next week. The other one, we haven't even posted.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Why not?

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Budget approval. It's been stuck with finance for a month.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: It'd be great if someone leaned on finance about that.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Is anyone else here thinking about leaving? Asking for a friend.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Hang on— Oskar.

turns.speaker: Carmen
turns.text: Okay, that's a conversation for a one-on-one.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: I'll set up a one-on-one with Oskar for tomorrow morning.

turns.speaker: Oskar
turns.text: Sure. Okay.

turns.speaker: Rachel
turns.text: Okay. Sprint ends November twenty-first. Let's actually finish it this time.

turns.speaker: Dev
turns.text: Famous last words.
